verified_by: 4-state differential (Maven 3.9.11, JDK 11) on a clean clone of openmrs/openmrs-core, using the project's OWN pre-existing test

discovery.found_by: bbc_e2e.py run (32-term deep mine, 2026-08-06) -> classify -> verify_traversal
discovery.note: Found only by the BUMP-axis search terms added in the 32-term mine; the earlier 3-query adaptation-signature corpus never surfaced it.

behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: From 1.4.18 XStream ships a deny-by-default type permission set. OpenMRS's SimpleXStreamSerializer constructed a plain `new XStream()` and deserialized arbitrary OpenMRS types; under 1.4.20 every such type is refused at deserialization time unless explicitly allowed. The code compiles unchanged and throws only at run time -> behavioural, not syntactic. Confirmed by the compile screen (verdict: behavioural, all 4 constructor usages still exist at 1.4.19).

adaptation.message: TRUNK-6188 Upgrade xstream and migrate to whitelisting (#4377)
adaptation.summary: Replace the permissive `new XStream()` with a whitelist mechanism driven by OpenMRS global properties. SimpleXStreamSerializer becomes a Spring @Component taking an AdministrationService, and setupXStreamSecurity() installs allowTypes / allowTypeHierarchy entries from AdministrationService.getSerializerWhitelistTypes(), supporting both exact types and a hierarchy-prefix form.

traversal.note: Rule 5 satisfied: the bump 1.4.17 -> 1.4.20 is in the adaptation commit itself, crossing the 1.4.18 boundary. Bundled shape is expected here and does NOT imply a compile break -- the compile screen returned `behavioural`, and state 2 below proves the parent source compiles fine against 1.4.20 and fails only at run time.

verification.method: Clean clone; xstream version varied by editing the single hardcoded <version> in the parent pom's dependencyManagement; JDK 11 (pom sets javaCompilerVersion 1.8); `mvn -pl api -am test` restricted to the single pre-existing test. Local repo -Dmaven.repo.local=C:/bump-p4p/.bbc_m2.
verification.settings_note: Required a project-local settings.xml. The machine's global ~/.m2/settings.xml declares <mirrorOf>*</mirrorOf> (added for an unrelated ORCID project), which routes every download through Central and so blocks OpenMRS's own Nexus -- the only source of jackson-{core,mapper}-asl:1.9.14-MULE-002 and ehcache:2.10.10.4.43. Mirroring only `central` fixes it without touching global config.

states.name: 4_adapted_production_with_PARENT_test
states.config: adapted production code (f8232475) + the PARENT's test file + xstream 1.4.20
states.purpose: Isolates whether the PRODUCTION change alone resolves this particular test.

verification.conclusion: Confirmed behavioural break. A test that passed at 1.4.17 fails at 1.4.20 with otherwise-unchanged code, throwing inside the production SimpleXStreamSerializer, and passes again after the adaptation commit.
verification.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT: State 4 shows this specific test's recovery is TEST-SIDE. The adaptation added `serializer.getXstream().allowTypeHierarchy(Foo.class)` to the test, and without that line the adapted production code still refuses Foo -- because the production whitelist is driven by OpenMRS global properties, which are absent in a plain unit test (adminService is null). So states 1->3 prove the BREAK and prove the client adapted, but do NOT by themselves prove the production change is what resolves it.

production_mechanism_separately_confirme.evidence: The full SimpleXStreamSerializerTest class on the adapted code: run=9 failures=0 errors=0.
production_mechanism_separately_confirme.why_it_matters: Those 9 include the commit's new tests deserialize_shouldNotDeserializeClassesThatAreNotWhitelisted and deserialize_shouldDeserializeWhitelistedPackages, which drive the production API directly -- `new SimpleXStreamSerializer(adminService)` with a mocked getSerializerWhitelistTypes() -- and assert both that non-whitelisted types are refused and that whitelisted packages deserialize. That is the production whitelist mechanism working, independent of any test-side allowTypeHierarchy call.
production_mechanism_separately_confirme.limitation: These are NEW tests, absent at the parent, so they cannot themselves form a 3-state differential (no baseline to pass).

assessment: A genuine production adaptation to a genuine behavioural break, in a large maintained project, with a confirmed in-repo boundary crossing. Stronger than the existing Axon demo-repo cases on project maturity. Weaker than them on one axis: the differential's state-3 recovery is attributable to a test-side line rather than to the production change, which state 4 makes explicit. The production mechanism is confirmed working by the commit's own new tests, just not by a 3-state differential.
